title: Miftah al-falah wa-misbah al-arwah (The Key to Salvation and the Lamp of Souls)
author: Ibn 'Ata' Allah al-Iskandari (d. 709/1309)

locator_hints: File line ~66-72: 'al-dhikr nar la tubqi wa-la tadhar': dhikr as fire that burns the body's surplus; where there is darkness it becomes light

File line ~95-112: stages tongue > heart > innermost (sirr); signs that dhikr has reached the sirr, incl. 'tara abadan anwaran sa'ida wa-ukhra nazila wa'l-niran hawalayka safiya' (you always see lights rising and others descending, and clear fires blazing around you)

Chapter on khalwa and its conditions; chapter on gradation of the Names (search 'الخلوة')
summary: The first full Arabic monograph on dhikr, by the third Shadhili master. It gives manners and method (purity, a dark or dim place, sitting with the head between the knees and the eyes closed, the sequence from spoken to heart to innermost invocation, choice of formula under a shaykh, retreat) and describes results in terms that include seen phenomena: dhikr is a fire that burns impurities and turns darkness to light; among the signs that the invocation has descended to the innermost is that its fires do not go out nor its lights depart, 'you always see lights ascending and others descending' with clear fires blazing around; visions of angels and prophets in beautiful forms come 'in the beginning' until one rises above the imaginal. The practitioner is told to report to the shaykh whatever he sees. Parts follow Kubra closely.
why_relevant: A dhikr manual with posture, eye closure and sequence, and stated visual signs of progress; shows the Kubrawi phenomenology absorbed into a mainstream Shadhili handbook. Seed lead confirmed.
